{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Algeria|Algerian Cuisine]]

'''Tamina''' ({{lang|ar|الطمينة}}) is a simple Algerian [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] mainly made of semolina. It is usually served during celebrations such as engagement parties, weddings, baby showers, or [[w:Mawlid|Mawlid]].

== Ingredients ==
* 500 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Semolina|semolina]] (medium-grind)
* 250 g melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
* 250 g [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Orange Flower Water|orange blossom water]] (mazhar)
* Ground [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (for decoration)
* [[Cookbook:Dragées|Dragées]] or [[Cookbook:Almond|almonds]] (for final decoration)

== Procedure ==
# Toast the semolina in a [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]] or in a cast iron dish until it takes on a nice golden color. Remove from the heat, and let it completely cool down.
# Melt the butter and honey in a [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], and add orange blossom water.
# Gradually add the cooled semolina while mixing.
# Cook for 3–5 minutes while stirring to combine everything well.
# Pour the tamina on a plate without waiting too long, and even out the surface.
# Sprinkle with cinnamon and garnish with almonds or dragées.
# Let cool and serve.
